🥄 Easy high protein breakfast idea that actually keeps you full

Here’s what you’ll need for 1 portion:

🫘 30g chia seeds
🍓 100g fruit
🥛 150g 0% Greek yogurt
🍼 200ml semi-skimmed milk
🍫 10g dark chocolate, cocoa nibs or peanut butter

Optional bits: honey, vanilla, cinnamon

1️⃣ Mix everything together
2️⃣ Chill in the fridge for 4+ hours
3️⃣ Add your fave toppings and enjoy

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
1 pot contains:
400 cals | 33g protein | 33g carbs | 17g fat
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Drop this in your meal prep rotation if you want something fast, filling, and high in protein.

You think you’re eating enough fiber? 🤔

Spinach, grapes, cucumber salad… all super healthy ✅
But when it comes to FIBER, looks can be deceiving 👀

🍫 1 square of 100% dark choc = 1 handful of spinach
🍇 Grapes <1g vs Raspberries 7g (10x more)
🥒 Salad (200g) = 1.7g vs 1 tbsp chia = 4g+
🥕 Courgette 1g vs Carrot nearly 3g
🍉 Huge slice of watermelon = teaspoon of oats

⚡️ 90% of people miss the 30g daily target.
Fiber = fullness, blood sugar control, gut health, longevity.

Don’t just add “random veg” — be smart with your portions. More fiber = better results.

videos.text:
What I Eat in a Day as a Doctor

This is a very important post for me because you need to understand that nutrition does not need to be overcomplicated. As you can see from the video, I eat a ton of lean meats, plenty of berries, and lots of vegetables. I keep my meals balanced, and when I portion my plate it is typically 40 percent protein, 40 percent fiber, and 20 percent carbohydrates.

I stick to a high-protein, high-fiber, lower-carb diet built on whole, clean foods. No processed junk. Every day I meal prep, hydrate, fast, sleep well, and train.

These aren’t hacks. They are the fundamentals every human needs to feel and perform their best. I’ve relied on these habits through medical school, residency, and even while balancing 60 to 70 hour work weeks with social media full-time.

Meal prepping is the foundation. If weight loss or better health is your goal, your food has to come first. Ninety percent of results start in the kitchen. Be consistent 80 percent of the time, and you can still enjoy the foods you love.

At the end of the day, there are no shortcuts and no excuses, just daily choices that build lifelong health.

What I eat in a day as a nutritionist 

For breakfast, I made my frozen fruit high fibre crumble. For me protein and fibre are king when it comes to building healthy meals. This version is so quick and easy, using a frozen summer berry fruit mix which is full of antioxdants and the crumble top is a mix of jumbo oats, brown sugar, egg whites,cashew butter, but you can use any nut butter, cinnamon and salt. bake until golden and bubbling and the top goes so crisp from the egg whites. Serve with a high protein yoghurt. 

For lunch is was my high protein tuna cottage cheese melts. Honestly, I need to create my own cottage cheese brand by this point but I really do find it so useful to boost protein in meals and it makes things taste SO good too with its rich creamy texture. A mix of tuna, cottage cheese, sweet corn, spring onions, fresh parsely, jalapenos and smoked chedder. this mix is prepable too and will hold for 3 days. load into your carb of choice, grill until oozing.

For dinner it was my super greens leek and parmesean pasta. Leeks are in season right now and taste so sweet and gorgeous. This is a really quick pasta recipe to make and I also had the left overs for lunch the next day. 

Finally my favourite hot chocolate and chocolate bar and I was well fed and ready for bed.

Are you on GLP-1 meds? These 5 common nutrition mistakes might be slowing your progress—and I’m  here to help you fix them!
1️⃣Eating "whatever you want": Skipping fiber and protein can lead to constipation, fatigue, and muscle loss. Prioritize veggies, lean proteins, and high-fiber carbs.
2️⃣ Skipping meals: Even without hunger, your
body needs fuel. Balanced meals or high-protein snacks keep energy steady and metabolism strong.
3️⃣Over-restricting calories: Eating too little (under 1,000 calories) can lead to muscle breakdown and unsustainable habits. Balance is key!
4️⃣Not staying hydrated: Sip water or try teas and sparkling water to stay hydrated and energized.
5️⃣Not planning ahead: Without meal prep, unhealthy choices or expensive takeout happen. A little planning goes a long way!
